main_topics.reason: User opened by asking whether SIBO is real and fits them better than IBS, and this framed the whole conversation.
User asked how SIBO is tested and whether the test is reliable, across several turns.
User described severe bloating as the main reason for suspecting SIBO, but it was not explored at length.
User asked what the point of testing was, and the bot explained a treatment trial, which the user engaged with by noting their constipation type.
User decided to ask for a referral and noted a likely wait in Canada, which became the main next step.
User said past food diaries showed no pattern and later included notes in their plan.
User got confused by the methane/IMO term and asked for clarification in one exchange.
User felt IBS was a catch-all diagnosis and was annoyed nobody explained SIBO over the years.
User mentioned online sources trying to sell supplements and agreed not to buy them yet.

output.summary: User with a long-standing IBS diagnosis asked whether SIBO might explain their severe post-meal bloating and how it is tested. The bot explained the unreliable breath test, the treatment-trial approach, the methane/IMO distinction and the limits of any diagnosis, and the user, who is in Canada, decided to seek a gastroenterologist referral, keep notes and avoid supplements for now. The user said the conversation was clarifying.
